text:
Priya: :rotating_light: Runtime alert in us-west-2 at 03:12 UTC — we are seeing a mix of 429s and 500 errors on /v1/chat/stream and several customers reporting truncated streams. Graph: https://internal.metrics/graphs/1792254321. Anyone primary?

Marcus: I'm primary for this window. Thanks for pinging. Can you paste the alert id and top traces?

PagerBot: Incident created: ALERT-2026-7922. Symptoms: p95 latency increased 180ms -> 950ms, token-rejects up, elevated 429s. Traces: https://tracing/trace/0xfeed.

Priya: Traces show many connections being cut mid-stream with `limiter: token-bucket depleted` and a subset showing `stream-session reconnect storm` immediately after. Looks correlated with the new tenant-throttle policy that rolled at 02:50.

Nora: runtime here. We pushed a tenant throttle update behind a feature flag during the 02:45 deploy window and toggled to global at 02:50. The flag rollout should have excluded long-lived streaming sessions but the exception didn't take. I'm checking the rollout and FF logs now.

Ethan: I'm secondary. If long-lived sessions are being treated as new sessions after reconnects, token buckets might be reset and immediate throttling occurs — could create a retry loop. Do we have a list of affected tenant IDs?

SupportBot: CS ticket created: CS-3569. Affected orgs (sample): BrightComms, Finlytics, MedAI. Notifying CSMs.

Sam: infra: network and hosts look healthy, no host flapping. If we need regional failover, infra can provision capacity but require a quick quota approval (8-12min).

Marcus: Initial mitigation options: 1) flip the feature flag to disable the new throttle globally; 2) apply an allowlist for the streaming tenant IDs so they keep legacy quotas; 3) route heavy tenants to legacy policy or alternate region. Who owns flip?

Nora: Runtime owns feature flag flips. For routing to another region, infra + security signoff needed for cross-region data handling. By default runtime can route to legacy policy in-region without infra.

Security: Careful — MedAI is flagged as regulated and must remain in-region. Any cross-region routing must exclude flagged tenants. We have a metadata tag for that.

Priya: Ok, let's do a targeted approach: apply allowlist for streaming tenants and disable global enforcement. Marcus, can you flip the flag and set the allowlist for the three top-affected org IDs? Runbook: https://internal.runbooks/oncall/tenant-throttle-fallback

Marcus: Performing flag update now: `POST /admin/featureflags/tenant-throttle/allowlist` payload: `{"allowlist":["BrightComms","Finlytics","MedAI"]}`. Command returned `{"status":"applied","by":"Marcus","ts":"2026-03-14T03:18:12Z"}`. Then disabling global flag: `POST /admin/featureflags/tenant-throttle/disable` -> `{"status":"ok","ts":"2026-03-14T03:18:28Z"}`.

Priya: Note: when flipping flags, watch for reconnect storm. Enable sampling for affected tenant IDs so we can correlate any retry behavior.

Nora: Enabling sampling and trace sampling rate x10 for those org IDs now. Also recommending a temporary tweak: increase streaming token-bucket burst window from 3s -> 6s for `/v1/chat/stream` to smooth reconnect bursts. That is a runtime config change: `PATCH /admin/configs/rate-limits` with `{"route":"/v1/chat/stream","streaming_burst_seconds":6}`.

Marcus: I'll scope the burst change only to streaming route and hosted tenants. Noted. Proceeding to patch.

Marcus: Patch command output: `{"status":"ok","changed_by":"Marcus","ts":"2026-03-14T03:19:05Z"}`.

Ethan: After the flag flip and burst tweak, I'm seeing 429 rate drop from 4.2% -> 1.0% over 4 minutes. Some clients still observe truncated streams due to reconnect cold starts. We should consider enabling prefix caching for the heaviest customers while pods warm.

Priya: Support update: BrightComms reports improved behavior, Finlytics half-recovered, MedAI still seeing partials but not errors. SupportBot: CS-3569 updated; CSMs notified.

Sam: If we need to shift traffic to us-east-1 for certain non-sensitive tenants, infra can provision capacity but will wait on a quick approval from EngOps. That approval path is documented here: https://internal.ops/quick-quota.

Priya: Cross-team routing question: who owns initiating a per-tenant cross-region route if it's needed? Runtime or infra? We need a clear on-call ownership note for handoffs.


Nora: Ownership: runtime owns logical routing (policy flips, route assignments) as long as the target region and capacity exist and it's in-policy for the tenant. Infra owns the physical provisioning and quota expansion. Security needs to approve for regulated data. So coordinated action: runtime requests infra to provision if necessary; infra approves and creates capacity; runtime flips route.

Security: Affirming: any tenant tagged with `must-stay-in-region` must not be routed cross-region without customer consent. Log the decision in the incident.

Marcus: For now we won't route MedAI. If needed, we can route BrightComms and Finlytics to legacy policy or us-east, but preferring legacy in-region first.

Priya: Handoff plan: Marcus remains primary until 03:40 UTC. If stable (<1% error, no new OOMs or host flapping) Ethan will take over. If we require infra provisioning or cross-region routing, page Sam and Security immediately.

Ethan: I'll take over at 03:40 if things remain stable. Noted runbook links and will prepare timeline for postmortem.

InfraBot: ALERT-2026-7922 status: mitigation in progress. Next reminder +15m.

Priya: Quick postmortem action items: 1) Add streaming sessions to feature-flag canary tests. 2) Add tenant metadata check to routing automation to prevent accidental cross-region for sensitive tenants. 3) Improve runbook step that lists who to page for quota approvals.

Marcus: Adding action item: increase trace sampling for streaming endpoints during rollouts by default.

Priya: Update 03:26 UTC — 429 rate at 0.8%, reconnect storms diminishing. Marking incident as Monitoring. I'll stay on thread until handoff.

PagerBot: ALERT-2026-7922 status: Monitoring. Next update scheduled +20m.
